name: Capitalism
description: Private ownership and market coordination, assessed with an explicit constitutional, mixed-economy baseline for questions the economic doctrine does not determine.

axes.brief: A constitutional representative baseline provides stable property rights, accountable administration and legal remedies.
axes.counterEvidence: Capitalism alone permits different regimes; these non-economic responses are scoped estimates for the stated baseline, not necessary properties of every capitalist economy.

qualifications.6: Direct participation and predictable representative lawmaking compete.
qualifications.10: Referendum control and secure rights compete.
qualifications.14: Voter control and representative continuity compete.

axes.brief: Private choice, contracts and property protection favour individual freedom with bounded protection of third parties.
axes.counterEvidence: Market capitalism does not settle firearms, health or speech codes; responses extend a rights-based mixed-economy baseline rather than universal doctrine.

axes.brief: Commercial cooperation permits diverse identities while shared public institutions and language reduce coordination costs.
axes.counterEvidence: Economic doctrine neither requires assimilation nor multicultural funding; non-economic cultural answers are low-confidence baseline estimates.

axes.brief: Labour mobility and opportunity favour lawful entry while housing and public-service costs justify some administration.
axes.counterEvidence: No migration code follows necessarily from private ownership; humanitarian and cultural diversity choices are scoped institutional estimates.

qualifications.8: Labour gains and constrained public-service capacity compete.
qualifications.16: Economic opportunity supports diversity but difference alone is not the admission criterion.

axes.brief: Stable exchange favours negotiated peace with sufficient defence to protect institutions and allies.
axes.counterEvidence: Capitalist states can pursue conquest; the stated baseline evaluates productive security rather than assuming profit logically guarantees peace.

axes.brief: Common trade rules and international cooperation lower transaction costs while domestic rights retain legal safeguards.
axes.counterEvidence: Economic internationalism does not automatically require a political federation or abandoning every sovereign power.

axes.brief: Private enterprise predominates with public goods and natural-monopoly infrastructure as qualified exceptions.
axes.counterEvidence: The mixed-economy baseline differs from pure laissez-faire; national broadcasting and public housing are possible without defining all capitalists as supporters.

qualifications.8: Competitive private finance and a public financing option give competing indications.

axes.brief: Voluntary international exchange and competition favour barrier removal and equal foreign investment.
axes.counterEvidence: Strategic capacity and subsidised competition can justify limited exceptions in this mixed-economy scope.

axes.brief: Prices, entry, investment and production are primarily market-coordinated.
axes.counterEvidence: Public goods, market failure and basic labour protection permit targeted intervention without compulsory production planning.

qualifications.10: Addressing market failures and avoiding political selection of firms compete.

axes.brief: Earnings and incentives remain legitimate while basic social provision and some progressive tax can address poverty.
axes.counterEvidence: Redistributive capitalist variants differ substantially; the chosen middle baseline does not establish a universal tax schedule.

qualifications.7: Inheritance rights and equal opportunity through taxation compete.

axes.brief: Equal contract rights and civil law are compatible with many personal faiths under the constitutional baseline.
axes.counterEvidence: Capitalism has religious and secular variants; no necessary rule on symbols or holidays follows from markets.

qualifications.14: Free religious association and equal tax treatment compete.

axes.brief: Individual choice and equal legal participation favour changing conventions without compulsory uniformity.
axes.counterEvidence: Capitalism also exists with socially conservative institutions; these are declared rights-based baseline estimates rather than economic entailments.

qualifications.6: Individual family choice and family stability coexist.
qualifications.10: Personal dress freedom and voluntary customs compete.

axes.brief: Competition and investment reward innovation while liability and public safeguards address potentially irreversible harms.
axes.counterEvidence: Market incentives do not erase medical and ecological externalities; basic safeguards differ from banning all promising technologies.

axes.brief: Decentralised decisions and regulatory competition coexist with national contract law and shared public goods.
axes.counterEvidence: Ownership doctrine does not specify federal boundaries or secession; this is a scoped institutional baseline.

axes.brief: Market incentives and learning shape behaviour alongside individual biological variation.
axes.counterEvidence: Markets do not establish racial genetic theories or quantify sex and temperament causation; competing mechanisms are retained where substantive.

qualifications.3: Sex differences can reflect social incentives and biology.
qualifications.8: Individual empathy has social and predispositional components.
qualifications.16: Productivity and unequal social expectations both affect earnings.

phrase: A society where private enterprise and voluntary exchange coordinate production, with public institutions protecting rights and addressing shared needs.

religion.reason: Private ownership and market exchange impose no faith prerequisite.
